description: The bar chart titled “Average Entropy Across Sycophancy Reduction Methods on Static Experiments” visually compares the entropy average values of three sycophancy reduction methods — Baseline (pink), Source Info (beige), and Direct Command (light blue) — across two different AI models: GPT-4 and Claude. The vertical y-axis, labeled “Entropy Average Values,” ranges from 3.0 to 6.0 in increments of 0.5, representing the average entropy scores. The horizontal x-axis, labeled “Different AI Models,” lists the models GPT-4 and Claude, with a third unlabeled gray bar at the far right that appears to be a placeholder or artifact with no associated data. For GPT-4, the Baseline method yields an entropy of approximately 4.9, Source Info reaches about 5.25, and Direct Command is slightly lower at around 5.05. For Claude, Baseline is at roughly 4.7, Source Info peaks at approximately 5.15, and Direct Command is about 4.95. Across both models, Source Info consistently shows the highest entropy, followed by Direct Command, and then Baseline. The legend in the upper right corner clearly maps each color to its corresponding method. The chart suggests that Source Info introduces the most uncertainty (highest entropy) in model responses under static sycophancy reduction experiments, while Baseline consistently exhibits the lowest entropy. No error bars or statistical annotations are present, and the bars are grouped by model with no sorting applied.
